key_agent_trends: Model access is now a change-of-control risk: OpenAI is ending Cursor’s contract after the SpaceX deal and withholding future models, including Astra.
Agent leaderboards are being reset. Terminal-Bench 4.0 dropped saturated tasks, capped runs at 8 hours, and still has the best system under 52%.
Open-weight coding models are closing the agent gap. GLM-5.3 ranks third on Terminal-Bench 4.0 when run inside Claude Code.
Copyright fights are moving from books to music catalogs that train the same agent platforms enterprises buy.
Harness quality now matters as much as the model: the same checkpoint scores differently depending on Claude Code versus Codex versus Grok Build.

stories.headline: OpenAI will cut Cursor’s model access on Nov. 12 after SpaceX closed the Anysphere deal
stories.what_happened: OpenAI notified SpaceX that it will wind down the contract supplying OpenAI models to Cursor, with a proposed shutoff of November 12, 2026—the maximum notice in the agreement. The company said it cannot be confident SpaceX will honor its terms of service, citing past contract breaches by Musk-owned firms, and said Cursor will not receive future models including Astra. Cursor CEO Michael Truell said OpenAI models are about 5% of Cursor traffic and that talks continue; Anthropic said it will increase Claude compute inside Cursor. Musk replied that he “couldn’t care less.”
stories.why_it_matters: The largest coding-agent product is now a test of whether model vendors will keep serving a rival’s stack after an acquisition. Developers on bundled Cursor plans face a multi-model reshuffle; API-key users are unaffected.

stories.headline: Terminal-Bench 4.0: Opus 5 + Claude Code leads at 51.8% after the task set was reset
stories.what_happened: Terminal-Bench shipped version 4.0 with a 66-task set, recalibrated time/CPU/memory, a uniform 8-hour cap, 19 task fixes, and 8 saturated or low-quality tasks removed. Published scores pair model and harness: Claude Opus 5 with Claude Code at 51.8% ± 3.4%, Fable 5 with Claude Code at 44.5%, GLM-5.3 with Claude Code at 41.8%, and GPT-5.6 Sol with Codex at 37.3%.
stories.why_it_matters: Older terminal benches were saturating. 4.0 measures long-horizon agent work under resource limits and makes the harness part of the result, not a footnote.

stories.headline: Z.ai releases GLM-5.3 open weights for agentic coding and cyber defense
stories.what_happened: Z.ai published GLM-5.3 checkpoints on Hugging Face after a delayed safety review. The model shares GLM-5.2’s base and attributes gains to post-training: vendor tests claim about 50% better in-house coding scores, open-weight SOTA on Terminal Bench 3.0 and Agents’ Last Exam, 84.5% on CyberGym, and 54.4% on ExploitBench. Weights are available in BF16 and FP8 with a 1M-token context; Unsloth and others shipped local GGUF/MLX builds within a day.
stories.why_it_matters: A large open coder that is competitive inside Claude Code changes who can run long-horizon agents without a closed API. The same post-training jump that lifted coding also lifted exploit benchmarks, which is why weights were delayed.

stories.headline: Sony Music and Warner Chappell sue Anthropic over Claude training data
stories.what_happened: Sony Music Publishing, Warner Chappell, and other publishers filed suit late August 28 in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California against Anthropic and co-founders Dario Amodei and Benjamin Mann. The complaint alleges illegal torrenting, scraping, and downloading of tens of thousands of compositions to train Claude and seeks up to $150,000 per work plus CMI-removal damages. Anthropic said it disagrees and will defend itself. The case is separate from Anthropic’s earlier $1.5B book settlement and from prior music suits by BMG and others.
stories.why_it_matters: Agent products inherit training-data liability. A music-catalog case at statutory-maximum scale raises the legal cost of web-scale pretraining for any vendor selling Slack, CRM, or coding agents on the same models.
